1	package cli
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"errors"
6		"io"
7		"strings"
8		"time"
9	
10		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/api"
11		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/auth"
12		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/gitremote"
13		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/logging"
14		"github.com/entireio/cli/internal/coreapi"
15	)
16	
17	// currentRepoRefTimeout bounds currentRepoRef's control-plane lookup. The
18	// lookup is best-effort decoration (recap degrades to personal-only without
19	// it), so a stalled core must not hang the command — mirror
20	// expertsCellResolveTimeout.
21	const currentRepoRefTimeout = 5 * time.Second
22	
23	// runAuthenticatedActivityAPI runs fn with an authenticated client for the
24	// activity/recap surface. It prefers the caller's home entire-api cell (the same
25	// shared client the experts commands use), which serves the /me/* endpoints
26	// these commands call.
27	//
28	// Cell routing is a best-effort upgrade: any failure building the cell client —
29	// the region has no cell yet (ErrNoCellForJurisdiction), not logged in, or a
30	// discovery/exchange error — falls back to the data API, which also serves
31	// /me/* and yields the canonical auth errors (e.g. the "not logged in" hint).
32	// This keeps the migration transparent and non-regressive; non-obvious
33	// fallbacks are logged for diagnosis. Both backends expose the same /me/* paths,
34	// so fn is agnostic to which client it receives.
35	func runAuthenticatedActivityAPI(ctx context.Context, errW io.Writer, insecureHTTP bool, fn func(context.Context, *api.Client) error) error {
36		client, err := auth.NewEntireAPICellClient(ctx, insecureHTTP, nil)
37		if err != nil {
38			logCellClientFallback(ctx, err)
39			return runAuthenticatedDataAPI(ctx, errW, insecureHTTP, fn)
40		}
41		return fn(ctx, client)
42	}
43	
44	// logCellClientFallback records, at debug, that an activity/recap command fell
45	// back from the entire-api cell to the data API. The expected cases — the
46	// region has no cell yet, or the caller isn't logged in — aren't logged: they
47	// are normal during rollout and on first use, not diagnosable failures.
48	func logCellClientFallback(ctx context.Context, err error) {
49		if errors.Is(err, auth.ErrNoCellForJurisdiction) || errors.Is(err, auth.ErrNotLoggedIn) {
50			return
51		}
52		logging.Debug(ctx, "activity/recap: entire-api cell client unavailable, using data API", "error", err.Error())
53	}
54	
55	// forgeToMirrorProvider maps a gitremote forge identifier (e.g. "gh") to the
56	// upstream provider the control plane records mirrors under (e.g. "github").
57	// entire-api routing only supports GitHub mirrors today.
58	func forgeToMirrorProvider(forge string) (string, bool) {
59		switch strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(forge)) {
60		case "gh", mirrorCloneProviderGitHub:
61			return mirrorCloneProviderGitHub, true
62		default:
63			return "", false
64		}
65	}
66	
67	// currentRepoRef best-effort resolves the current repo (its "origin" remote)
68	// to the ULID entire-api uses for repo-scoped params — recap's /me/recap?repo=
69	// — plus the human owner/repo slug for display, from a single remote
70	// resolution (the caller needs both; resolving twice would double the git and
71	// control-plane work). entire.io/api documents the mirror id as exactly that
72	// repo_id (repo_id = mirror_repos.id), and the CLI already lists mirrors via
73	// the control plane, so no extra resolution is needed. Any failure returns
74	// "", "" — recap then shows the personal side only rather than erroring.
75	func currentRepoRef(ctx context.Context) (repoID, repoSlug string) {
76		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, currentRepoRefTimeout)
77		defer cancel()
78	
79		forge, owner, repo, err := gitremote.ResolveRemoteRepo(ctx, "origin")
80		if err != nil || owner == "" || repo == "" {
81			return "", ""
82		}
83		provider, ok := forgeToMirrorProvider(forge)
84		if !ok {
85			return "", ""
86		}
87		c, err := coreapi.New()
88		if err != nil {
89			return "", ""
90		}
91		mirrors, err := listMirrorsForRepo(ctx, c, provider, strings.ToLower(owner), repo)
92		if err != nil {
93			return "", ""
94		}
95		repoID = firstActiveRepoID(mirrors)
96		if repoID == "" {
97			return "", ""
98		}
99		return repoID, owner + "/" + repo
100	}
101	
102	// firstActiveRepoID returns the id of the repo's first active mirror (the repo
103	// id is stable across a repo's placements, so any active one serves). Archived
104	// and failed/suspended placements are skipped — they can't answer for the repo.

Stacked on #1592. Extracts the CLI's cell-routing plumbing into a shared foundation so multi-cell commands (code search, #1616, and anything after it) stop growing parallel copies of it. The backend model gives the CLI exactly three routing shapes, mirroring the entire.io BFF: repo-scoped → one cell, user-scoped /me → home cell, repo-set queries → fan out and merge client-side (no server-side aggregator exists). #1592 covers the second; this PR generalizes the first and builds the third.

## Commits

- **`auth.CellClientFactory`** — `NewEntireAPICellClient` resolved the login subject (discovery + refresh) and ran the RFC 8693 exchange on every call. Identity tokens are per-jurisdiction, not per-cell, so a fan-out over N cells was about to pay N× all of it. The factory resolves the subject once and mints at most one token per jurisdiction; `NewEntireAPICellClient` stays as the single-cell wrapper, existing callers unchanged.
- **`cell_target.go`** — mechanical generalization of `experts_cell_target.go` (`resolveRepoCellTarget`, `cellCoreClient`, `cellResolveTimeout`): nothing in it was experts-specific, and it's the repo-scoped shape every cell-routed command needs. No behavior change.
- **`cell_fanout.go`** — the repo-set shape, extracted from what #1616 currently inlines into `search_cmd.go`:
  - `groupReposByCell`: repo index → per-cell groups, deterministic order.
  - `resolveCellBaseURLs`: cluster-catalog join on `ClusterSlug`↔`Cluster.Slug`. The catalog exposes **no cell field** — #1616's current join of the cell name against `Slug` only works when the two happen to coincide; a test pins the correct key.
  - `fanOutCells`: parallel per-cell calls under a per-cell timeout through **one** shared `CellClientFactory`; partial failures are isolated per result slot, merge semantics stay with the command.
- Documents the three routing shapes in CLAUDE.md.

## Intended consumer

#1616 (code search) keeps its `codesearch` client, merge/sort/dedup semantics, and output rendering, and replaces its inline `groupReposByCell`/`searchAllCells`/`searchCell` orchestration with these helpers — fixing the slug join and the per-cell token minting along the way.

## Testing

`mise run test:ci` green (unit + integration + both canary suites), `-race` on the fan-out tests. New tests: factory token reuse per jurisdiction, group determinism, slug-join pinning, per-cell failure isolation.

101				// placement (the repo to read content FROM), and the resolved display.
102				type originGroup struct {
103					localPlacement string
104					fullName       string

106					checkpointIDs  []string

1	/**
2	 * Format a raw model identifier into a short display label.
3	 *
4	 * Examples:
5	 *   "claude-opus-4-6"        -> "Opus 4.6"
6	 *   "claude-sonnet-4-6"      -> "Sonnet 4.6"
7	 *   "claude-haiku-4-5"       -> "Haiku 4.5"
8	 *   "claude-sonnet-4-20250514" -> "Sonnet 4"
9	 *   "gpt-4o"                 -> "GPT-4o"
10	 *   "gemini-2.0-flash"       -> "Gemini 2.0 Flash"
11	 *
12	 * Unknown formats pass through unchanged.
13	 */
14	export function formatModel(model: string | null | undefined): string | null {
15	  if (!model) return null
16	  const trimmed = model.trim()
17	  if (!trimmed) return null
18	
19	  // Claude models: claude-<family>-<major>[-<minor>][-<YYYYMMDD>]
20	  // Date suffixes are 6+ digits; minor versions are short numerics.
21	  const claudeMatch = trimmed.match(/^claude-(opus|sonnet|haiku)-(\d+)(.*)$/i)
22	  if (claudeMatch) {
23	    const [, family, major, rest] = claudeMatch
24	    const familyLabel = family.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + family.slice(1).toLowerCase()
25	    const tailParts = rest.split("-").filter(Boolean)
26	    // A 6+ digit chunk is a date suffix — ignore everything from it onward.
27	    const minorParts: string[] = []
28	    for (const part of tailParts) {
29	      if (/^\d{6,}$/.test(part)) break
30	      minorParts.push(part)
31	    }
32	    const minor = minorParts.join(".")
33	    return minor ? `${familyLabel} ${major}.${minor}` : `${familyLabel} ${major}`
34	  }
35	
36	  // GPT models: gpt-4o, gpt-4-turbo, gpt-3.5-turbo
37	  if (/^gpt-/i.test(trimmed)) {
38	    return "GPT-" + trimmed.replace(/^gpt-/i, "")
39	  }
40	
41	  // Gemini: gemini-2.0-flash -> "Gemini 2.0 Flash"
42	  if (/^gemini-/i.test(trimmed)) {
43	    return trimmed
44	      .split("-")
45	      .map((part) => part.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + part.slice(1))
46	      .join(" ")
47	  }
48	
49	  return trimmed
50	}
